gp.text: Cost of Sales and Gross Margin – Our Chemicals Segment’s c ost of sales increased by $3.8 million, or 1%, in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025 due to the net effects of a 14% increase in sales volumes, higher energy costs, higher production rates resulting in reduced unabsorbed fixed production costs, lower raw material costs (primarily feedstock), and lower production costs resulting primarily from the cost reduction initiatives implemented in the fourth quarter of 2025. Our Chemicals Segment’s cost of sales in the third quarter of 2025 included approximately $27 million of unabsorbed fixed costs as it adjusted its TiO 2 production volumes lower to align inventory levels with lower demand. Unabsorbed fixed costs in the third quarter of 2026 were not material.

cor.text: Excluding the effects of changes in currency exchange rates, our Chemicals Segment’s cost of sales per metric ton of TiO 2 sold in the first nine months of 2026 was lower than the comparable period of 2025 due to decreases in per metric ton production costs, primarily driven by the cost reduction initiatives discussed above, as well as lower raw material costs (primarily feedstock costs) and lower unabsorbed fixed costs, partially offset by higher energy costs.

oi.text: We currently expect consolidated operating income for 2026 to be higher as compared to 2025 primarily due to the net effects of:

ga.text: Other General Corporate Items – Corporate expenses were 13% lower in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025 primarily due to lower general and administrative costs partially offset by higher environmental remediation and related costs. Corporate expenses were 8% lower in the first nine months of 2026 primarily due to lower general and administrative costs and lower environmental remediation and related costs. Included in corporate expense are:

nonop.text: Interest Expense – Interest expense decreased $1.1 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025 primarily due to lower overall average debt balances. Interest expense increased $1.3 million in the first nine months of 2026 compared

tax.text: Income Tax Expense – We recognized income tax expense of $8.0 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to income tax expense of $14.3 million in the third quarter of 2025 and income tax expense of $26.1 million in the first nine months of 2026 compared to $30.3 million in the first nine months of 2025. The decrease in the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 is primarily due to the impact of the change in our §987 currency translation gain as a result of proposed currency regulations issued in August 2026 and recognized in the third quarter of 2026 and the impact of the German federal tax rate change on our German net deferred tax asset recorded in the third quarter of 2025, partially offset by the higher earnings in 2026 and the jurisdictional mix of such earnings. During interim periods, our effective tax rate may not necessarily correspond to the current period income (loss) before taxes due to the application of accounting for income taxes in interim periods which requires us to base our effective rate on full year projections of pre-tax income (loss).

net.text: We reported net income attributable to Valhi stockholders of $30.2 million, or $1.06 per diluted share, in the third quarter of 2026 compared to a net loss attributable to Valhi stockholders of $22.2 million, or $.78 per diluted share, in the third quarter of 2025. Our net income attributable to Valhi stockholders increased from 2025 to 2026 primarily due to higher operating income from our Chemicals Segment of $60.5 million in 2026 compared to an operating loss of $15.9 million in 2025 partially offset by lower operating income from our Real Estate Management and Development Segment of $.5 million in 2026 compared to $19.7 million in 2025.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities –
ocf.text: Trends in cash flows from operating activities (excluding the impact of significant asset dispositions and relative changes in assets and liabilities) are generally similar to trends in our operating income. In addition to the impact of the operating, investing and financing cash flows discussed below, changes in the amount of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash we report from period to period can be impacted by changes in currency exchange rates, since a portion of our cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash is held by our non-U.S. subsidiaries.

capex.heading: Capital Expenditures and Other –
capex.text:
We currently expect our aggregate capital expenditures for 2026 will be approximately $65 million as follows:

In addition, LandWell expects to spend approximately $13 million on land development costs during 2026.

Capital spending for 2026 is expected to be funded through cash generated from operations or borrowing under our existing credit facilities. Planned capital expenditures for the remainder of 2026 at Kronos and CompX will primarily be to maintain and improve our existing facilities and, as it relates to CompX, to meet expected customer demand and maintain technology infrastructure. It is possible we will delay planned capital projects based on market conditions including but not limited to expected demand and the general availability of materials, equipment and supplies necessary to complete such projects.

Chemicals.heading: Chemicals –
Chemicals.text: We consider TiO 2 to be a “quality of life” product, with demand affected by gross domestic product, or GDP, and overall economic conditions in our markets located in various regions of the world. Over the long-term, we expect demand for TiO 2 will grow by 2% to 3% per year, consistent with our expectations for the long-term growth in GDP. However, even if our Chemicals Segment and its competitors maintain consistent shares of the worldwide market, demand for TiO 2 in any interim or annual period may not change in the same proportion as the change in GDP, in part due to relative changes in the TiO 2 inventory levels of our Chemicals Segment’s customers. We believe our Chemicals Segment’s customers’ inventory levels are influenced in part by their expectations for future changes in TiO 2 selling prices as well as their expectations for future availability of product.

Component products.heading: Component Products –
Component products.text:
Our Component Products Segment’s product offerings consist of a significantly large number of products that have a wide variation in selling price and manufacturing cost, which results in certain practical limitations on its ability to quantify the impact of changes in individual product sales quantities and selling prices on the segment’s net sales, cost of sales and gross margin. In addition, small variations in period-to-period net sales, cost of sales and gross margin can result from changes in the relative mix of our Component Products Segment’s products sold. The key performance indicator for our Component Products Segment is operating income .

Our Component Products Segment’s operating income in the third quarter of 2026 was $6.4 million compared to $4.8 million in the same period of 2025. Operating income for the first nine months of 2026 was $22.4 million compared to $17.0 million for the comparable prior year period.

Real estate management and development.heading: Real Estate Management and Development –
Real estate management and development.text:
General – Our Real Estate Management and Development Segment consists of BMI and LandWell. BMI and LandWell owned and developed real property in Henderson, Nevada. LandWell is actively engaged in developing a residential/planned community in Henderson.

LandWell began marketing land for sale in the residential/planned community in December 2013 and sold the last remaining parcel during 2025. In addition, adjacent to the residential/planned community, LandWell has been actively marketing and selling land zoned for commercial and light industrial use and sold the last of those remaining parcels during the first quarter of 2026. Although land sales may be completed, we do not recognize revenue until we have satisfied the criteria for revenue recognition. In some instances, LandWell received cash proceeds at the time the contract closed and recorded deferred revenue for some or all of the cash amount received, with such deferred revenue being recognized in subsequent periods. Although all of the land in the residential/planned community has been sold, we continue to complete our development obligations. We expect the development work to be completed by the end of 2027.

Net Sales and Operating Income – Substantially all of the net sales from our Real Estate Management and Development Segment in the third quarter and the first nine months of 2026 and 2025 were from land sales.

intro.text: Valhi, Inc. (NYSE: VHI) is primarily a holding company. We operate through our wholly-owned and majority-owned subsidiaries, including NL Industries, Inc., Kronos Worldwide, Inc., CompX International Inc., Basic Management, Inc. and The LandWell Company. Kronos (NYSE: KRO), NL (NYSE: NL) and CompX (NYSE American: CIX) each file periodic reports with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Our principal executive offices are located at Three Lincoln Center 5430 LBJ Freeway, Suite 1700, Dallas, Texas 75240-2620. Our telephone number is (972) 233-1700. We maintain a website at www.valhi.net.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: We believe Kronos is the largest TiO 2 producer and chloride process TiO 2 producer in Europe with 45% of its 2025 sales volumes attributable to markets in Europe.
Kronos sells to a diverse customer base with no single customer representing 10% or more of our Chemicals Segment’s net sales in 2025.
Our Component Products Segment sells to a diverse customer base with only one customer representing 10% or more of its consolidated net sales in 2025 (United States Postal Service – 26%).
Our Component Products Segment’s largest ten customers accounted for approximately 52% of its consolidated net sales in 2025.

During 2025 we had recognized revenue on land sales to three customers that exceeded 10% of our Real Estate Management and Development Segment’s net sales (DR Horton – 34%, Richmond American Homes – 12% and Lennar Homes – 12%) related to land sales.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, our Component Products Segment’s largest ten customers accounted for approximately 52% of its consolidated net sales, with a single customer accounting for 26% of its consolidated net sales.
Our Chemicals Segment’s revenue from non-U.S. markets accounted for approximately 66%, 66% and 64% of its revenue for the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively.

Land sales associated with the residential/planned community have variable consideration components which are based on a percentage of the builder’s ultimate selling price of a residential housing unit to their customer (ranging from 2.5 % to 3.5 % of such sales price).
During 2023, we recognized revenue from five customers that each exceeded 10 % of our Real Estate Management and Development Segment’s net sales all related to land sales.
During each of 2024 and 2025, we recognized revenue from three customers that each exceeded 10 % of our Real Estate Management and Development Segment’s net sales all related to land sales.
Kronos purchases feedstock for its chloride process TiO 2 from the following primary suppliers for volumes for delivery extending in some cases, through 2028:
Kronos relies upon unpatented proprietary knowledge and continuing technological innovation and other trade secrets to develop and maintain its competitive position.

These raw materials are purchased from several suppliers, are readily available from numerous sources and accounted for approximately 14% of our Component Products Segment’s total cost of sales for 2025.
Total material costs, including purchased components, represented approximately 43% of our Component Products Segment’s cost of sales in 2025.
Certain components used in our Component Products Segment’s products are manufactured by foreign suppliers located in China and elsewhere.
Our ability to make payments on and refinance our debt and to fund planned capital expenditures depends on our ability to generate cash flow in the future.

Our Component Products Segment relies on patent, trademark and trade secret laws in the United States and similar laws in other countries to establish and maintain our intellectual property rights in our technology and designs.
The ultimate impact of any tariffs will depend on various factors, including the length of time tariffs are ultimately implemented and the amount, scope and nature of the tariffs.

Our businesses rely on integrated information technology systems to manage, process and analyze data, including to facilitate the manufacture and distribution of products to and from our facilities, receive, process and ship orders, manage the billing of and collections from customers and manage payments to vendors.
The timing of payments depends upon a number of factors, including but not limited to the timing of the actual remediation process; which in turn depends on factors outside of our control.

NL – NL has been named as a defendant in various lawsuits in several jurisdictions, alleging personal injuries as a result of occupational exposure primarily to products manufactured by our former operations containing asbestos, silica and/or mixed dust.

General – Our Component Products Segment’s profitability primarily depends on its ability to utilize its production capacity effectively, which is affected by, among other things, the demand for its products and its ability to control its manufacturing costs, primarily comprised of labor costs and materials.
Total material costs represented approximately 43% of our Component Products Segment’s cost of sales in 2025, with commodity-related raw materials representing approximately 14% of its cost of sales.

Our primary source of liquidity on an ongoing basis is our cash flows from operating activities and borrowings under various lines of credit and notes.
Certain of our leases include variable lease payments that depend on a specified index or rate.
While our future global operations depend on a number of different factors, we do expect to have future U.S. inclusions in taxable income related to GILTI.

The issue of whether insurance coverage for defense costs or indemnity or both will be found to exist for our lead pigment and asbestos litigation depends upon a variety of factors and we cannot assure you that such insurance coverage will be available.

pti: Income (Loss) from Continuing Operations before Income Taxes, Noncontrolling Interest

s.t: During the third quarter of 2025, our Chemicals Segment recognized a non-cash gain of $ 4.6 million from the remeasurement of an earn-out liability associated with its 2024 acquisition of the remaining ownership interest in Louisiana Pigment Company, L.P. ("LPC").
During the first nine months of 2026, we recognized a $2.1 million non-cash deferred income tax benefit with respect to our direct investment in Kronos.

We recognize deferred income taxes with respect to the excess of the financial reporting carrying amount over the income tax basis of our direct investment in Kronos common stock because the exemption under GAAP to avoid such recognition of deferred income taxes is not available to us.

This benefit reflects a decrease in the deferred income taxes required to be recognized on the excess of the financial reporting carrying amount over the income tax basis of our direct investment in Kronos common stock and was related to our equity in Kronos’ net income during the period.

A portion of the net change with respect to the excess of the financial reporting carrying amount over the income tax basis of our direct investment in Kronos common stock during such periods related to our equity in Kronos’ other comprehensive income (loss) items, and the amounts allocated to other comprehensive income (loss) items includes amounts related to our equity in Kronos’ other comprehensive income (loss) items.

The amount shown for incremental tax benefit on investment in BMI/LandWell represents current and deferred income taxes associated with distributions and earnings from our investment in BMI and LandWell.
At December 31, 2025, we recognized a deferred income tax liability with respect to our direct investment in Kronos of $49.7 million.
There is a maximum amount (or cap) of such deferred income taxes we are required to recognize with respect to our direct investment in Kronos.
All of our ownership interest in CompX is held through our ownership in NLI; as such we do not receive any dividends from CompX.

s.t: Gain on Remeasurement of Investment in TiO 2 Manufacturing Joint Venture – We recognized a gain on the remeasurement of Kronos’ investment in LPC of $64.5 million in the third quarter of 2024 as a result of the acquisition.

We recognize deferred income taxes with respect to the excess of the financial reporting carrying amount over the income tax basis of our direct investment in Kronos common stock because the exemption under GAAP to avoid such recognition of deferred income taxes is not available to us.

During 2025, we recognized a non-cash deferred income tax benefit with respect to our direct investment in Kronos of $ 7.5 million for the decrease in the deferred income taxes required to be recognized with respect to the excess of the financial reporting carrying amount over the income tax basis of our direct investment in Kronos common stock, to the extent such decrease related to our equity in Kronos’ net income during such period.

A portion of the net change with respect to the excess of the financial reporting carrying amount over the income tax basis of our direct investment in Kronos common stock during such periods related to our equity in Kronos’ other comprehensive income (loss) items, and the amounts shown in the table above for income tax expense (benefit) allocated to other comprehensive income (loss) items includes amounts related to our equity in Kronos’ other comprehensive income (loss) items.

Such pre-tax gain is disclosed as gain on remeasurement of investment in TiO 2 manufacturing joint venture and is included in cost and other expense (income) in our Consolidated Statement of Operations.
Tremont LLC – Tremont is primarily a holding company through which we hold our 63% ownership interest in BMI and our 77% ownership interest in LandWell.
Our 77% ownership interest in LandWell includes 27% we hold through our ownership of Tremont and 50% held by a subsidiary of BMI.
All of our ownership interest in CompX is held through our ownership in NL; as such we do not receive any dividends from CompX.

We accounted for our investment in Louisiana Pigment Company, L.P. (“LPC”), which was operated as a 50 %-owned manufacturing joint venture, by the equity method before Kronos’ acquisition of the remaining 50 % joint venture interest in July 2024.

The amount shown for incremental tax benefit on investment in BMI/LandWell represents current and deferred income taxes associated with distributions and earnings from our investment in BMI and LandWell.
At December 31, 2025, we have recognized a deferred income tax liability with respect to our direct investment in Kronos of $ 49.7 million.
There is a maximum amount (or cap) of such deferred income taxes we are required to recognize with respect to our direct investment in Kronos.
We have recognized deferred income taxes for our investment in Kronos common stock.
